item: Row 416: one worker pool for the whole re-index drain, memory-bounded
summary: precompute_batch built a process pool per 500-article window and every new worker reloaded its dictionaries (about 4.4 s CPU per worker per mixed-language window). DrainPool keeps one pool for the drain, recycles it after 50,000 articles, kills a broken pool and computes that window serially (the ruled fallback) with a fresh pool next window, and bounds workers by free memory ((available - 1,536 MiB) / 750 MiB per worker, kept workers added back; below two the window runs serially and the pool is released). Exclusive import workers: max(2, cores - 1). Measured, mixed 12-language corpus, identical output digests: 21-window drain on 2 cores 32.0 to 46.1 articles/s, and 32.1 to 46.9 under a 4 GB cgroup cap (peak 1,936 vs 1,924 MB, no OOM); worker RSS 686 to 703 MB over a 58-window drain. Engine pins kept with --same (golden output digest unchanged).
